🧠 Core Context Brain - Build the shared knowledge foundation
Run Deep Research on School Technology Associates Do now
Opens the Deep Research project and run a full multi-source company research session on STA. This populates knowledge-base/sta/sta-company-profile/ with structured topic modules covering company overview, product line, team, customers, partnerships, recent activity, and market position. A seed doc (context-files/shared/sta-company-profile.md) already exists from web research done 2026-04-29 - Deep Research extends and deepens it.
Exact prompt (paste into Deep Research):
Research School Technology Associates, Inc. (k12sta.com) comprehensively. Produce structured KB modules covering each of the following areas:

1. Company Overview - founding history, mission, headquarters, size, revenue estimates, ownership structure, notable facts
2. Product Line - full catalog with descriptions, target buyer per product, integrations, pricing model (quote-based vs. listed), any recent launches (note: VirtuaTime launched March 2026)
3. Team & Leadership - all named staff with titles, founder background (Dan Hoerl), org structure inferences
4. Customer Base - named districts, geographic spread, customer segments (public district vs. private/Catholic), testimonial themes
5. Partnership Ecosystem - Skyward relationship (exclusive partner - when did this start?), WSIPC, eFunds, Region 19, ISCorp (SchoolTRAK hosting), Attendance Works
6. Market Position - who else sells Skyward-integrated hardware/software, how STA differentiates, conference presence (Skyward user groups PA/KS/WI), competitive gaps
7. Recent Activity - last 90 days of news, LinkedIn posts, blog posts, product announcements, conference appearances
8. Online Presence - website, LinkedIn, social channels, podcast, Help Center (Salesforce), SEO footprint

Sources to hit: k12sta.com (all pages including /about-us/, /products/, /news/, /events/), LinkedIn company page, web search for press mentions and reviews, Skyward partner directory if accessible, any K-12 ed-tech industry databases. Use Harmonic to enrich company and people profiles if available.

Save as separate modules per topic area in knowledge-base/sta/sta-company-profile/.
Note: Install the Harmonic MCP connector first if available (search MCP registry for "harmonic") - it enriches LinkedIn-derived people and company data without requiring a LinkedIn login.
Distill Deep Research output into core context-shared files Do now
After Deep Research completes, open The Architect and run the knowledge-base-context-builder skill on the output modules. Target: produce the following 7 files in context-files/shared/:
  • sta-company-profile.md - already seeded; update with Deep Research findings
  • sta-brand-identity.md - tone, voice, brand colors, writing style, logo rules
  • sta-products-catalog.md - full product list with buyer targets and Skyward integration details
  • sta-team-roster.md - complete team, titles, responsibilities, contact emails
  • sta-customers-icp.md - named districts, customer segments, ideal customer profile
  • sta-tech-stack.md - all systems STA runs (Skyward, Salesforce, WooCommerce, Mailchimp, etc.)
  • sta-partnerships.md - Skyward exclusive history, WSIPC, eFunds, Region 19, ISCorp, Attendance Works
Files marked "needs internal input" in the New Project Build Guide Core Brain table require follow-up with the relevant team member before they are complete. See that doc for details on who to ask for each gap. Full spec: New Project Build Guide V2.html, Core Brain section.
Refresh core context files when company info changes Recurring
When STA's products change (new launch, deprecated product), team changes (hire, departure, title change), customer base expands significantly, or a partnership changes - update the relevant file(s) in context-files/shared/. Then re-upload the updated file to any Claude.ai Projects that use it. Cowork projects read the files live and pick up changes automatically. Target cadence: review all 7 core context files quarterly, or immediately after any major company change.

Periodically clear out old Cowork workspaces Recurring
Every month or two, open Cowork and review your workspace list. Close or delete any workspace that is: deprecated, replaced by a newer version, or one you have not used in 60+ days. Stale workspaces consume context and cause confusion when their names overlap with active ones. The Prompt Maker is the first - others will accumulate over time. When in doubt, archive rather than delete.
